topics.title: Political Theory: Its Roots and Objectives

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how reason, reflection and language form the roots of political theory.
State what political theory examines and its objective of training citizens to think rationally.
Distinguish the negative popular image of politics from politics as a worthwhile and integral activity.
Explain politics as negotiation and collective decision making at the level of government and of people.
Identify the contributions of major political thinkers to ideas such as freedom and equality.
Describe how political theory clarifies concepts and probes principles that shape constitutions and social life.

topics.title: Why Questions of Freedom and Equality Persist

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why values guaranteed formally may not be realised equally in all spheres of life.
Explain how constitutional rights are reinterpreted and expanded in response to new circumstances.
Analyse new opportunities and threats to freedom created by communication technology and the internet.
Explain why political concepts have many definitions unlike mathematical terms.
Describe how Socrates used reason to reveal the limitations of a given view of justice.
Analyse how the meaning of equality changes with context, from equal opportunity to special provisions and fair distribution.

topics.title: Why Should We Study Political Theory?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why political theory is useful for students, professionals and voting citizens.
Evaluate how political theory helps us examine our prejudices and debate rationally.
